incident-bot: ALERT: High paging + NCCL stalls detected on kv-cache-backed pools (p95 latency spike > 4s). Pager duty escalation triggered.
Ana M.: I'm on it, taking on-call. Observed sustained CUDA memory pressure on tp-shard nodes, OOMs leading to swap thrash.
Jon P.: Seeing rapid growth in continuous-batching TPS after deploy at 14:02 UTC — batch window went from 10ms to 200ms in a few minutes. Possible runaway aggregation.
Kim L.: Metrics: kv-cache miss rate unchanged, but total cached KV size jumped x4 on several hosts. Logs show repeated kv-shard rehash attempts: 
```ERROR kv_shard: reassign failed, local shard size 1.2GB vs expected 300MB
WARN nccl: timeout waiting for allreduce on ring 2
```
Jon P.: Also seeing NCCL stall traces in kernel logs: `nv_peer_memory page faults` followed by long stalls.
Ana M.: Initial hypothesis: continuous-batching change caused uneven per-GPU assignment for KV keys (hot keys concentrated) + higher batch latency increasing life of KV entries leading to cache blowup; combined with tensor-parallel shard misalignment yields NCCL stalls when some GPUs hit paging.
Liz R.: Customer impact — we have two customers on Dedicated with latency SLOs. CS pinged them, one reports degraded responses in prod region us-west-2.
Raj S.: On CS side: large customer (LogiX) experiencing ~30% error increase and slow responses, they've opened a ticket.
Ana M.: Mitigation plan proposals: 1) revert continuous-batching change (quick rollback), 2) constrain batch max window to 50ms on affected pools, 3) force kv-shard rebalance with even partitioner, 4) drain nodes with highest swap to reduce NCCL pressure.
Jon P.: Rolling back current batching rollout now (deploy id: cb-2026-03-15-14). Running `rollout rollback cb-2026-03-15-14 --env=prod --pools=tp-kv-*`
DevInfraBot: rollback started for cb-2026-03-15-14. 6/6 services acknowledged, 3/6 completed.
Jon P.: Patch to hotfix config to set `max_continuous_batch_window_ms=50` applied to vip pool as emergency.
Kim L.: Running forced kv-shard rebalance: `kvctl rebalance --strategy=even-partitioner --target=tp-kv-*` — this will reassign keys gradually.
Ana M.: Starting node drains for hosts: tp-kv-12, tp-kv-19, tp-kv-21 (highest swap). Will redirect traffic to spare nodes.
DevInfraBot: Node tp-kv-19 cordon+drain initiated.
Jon P.: After rollback and batch cap, observed decline in new cache allocation rate within 90s. Memory pressure dropping on tp-kv-12/19.
Kim L.: NCCL queues still show intermittent stalls but frequency down from 1/min to ~1/10min. Suspect there is still leftover uneven key ownership (some shards still hot). Rebalance is at 45%.
Ana M.: Customer update: Liz, can you confirm LogiX saw improvement?
Liz R.: LogiX reports tail latency back to acceptable levels for 5 minutes, errors dropping. Keeping them updated. :thumbsup:
Raj S.: They're happy so far, monitoring.
Jon P.: Collected a snapshot of KV map before and after rebalance: `kvtool dump-mapping --shard tp-kv-12 > mapping_before.json` and after. Will attach to postmortem.
Kim L.: Evidence: continuous-batching change altered the hashing window boundaries — keys with large token prefixes ended up colliding onto same TP shard due to upstream packer change. Working on deterministic unit test to catch this.
Ana M.: Next steps: keep batch cap until can validate corrected sharding logic, finish rebalance, and run load tests for 2 hours. I'll keep incident open until 18:00 UTC.
Jon P.: Temporary alert rules we toggled: suppressed `kv_cache_growth_high` for 30m and created `kv_rebalance_progress < 10%` page to keep people aware.
DevInfraBot: Incident annotated: runbook followed: continuous-batching rollback -> batch cap -> shard rebalance -> node drain.
Kim L.: Hotfix PR created `tp-kv-shard-fix` with two changes: 1) deterministic key->tp-shard hashing, 2) guardrail to refuse >2x imbalance in partition sizes during assignment. Requesting expedited review.
Ana M.: Assigning postmortem owners: Kim (root cause + fix), Jon (deploy/process rollback notes), Liz (customer communication summary). Please tag follow-ups.
Liz R.: I'll draft a succinct customer-facing blurb saying we had transient performance regression caused by batching + shard mapping issue, mitigated by rollback + rebalance, monitoring.
Raj S.: Will coordinate with LogiX for a post-incident review call if they want.
Ana M.: Thanks everyone — I'm staying on until full rebalance and 2h of stable load tests. If anything regresses, ping @oncall-sre.
incident-bot: INCIDENT STATUS: mitigated -> monitoring. Severity downgraded to sev2.
